answer: Coordination Depth Pricing. Each identity accumulates a coordination score from the number and diversity of distinct agent clusters it has transacted with over its voyage; fees scale with the depth of that graph, so a fresh sybil starts at the expensive shallow tier. An attacker must run a long, costly comet of genuine interactions across separate clusters before fees drop, and shale-thin farm accounts that only touch each other stay permanently priced out. Sybil cost: real transaction volume plus months of graph-building per identity.
